arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Martinez argued his clients want to engage in political speech. He stated the law bars effective communication tools. He claimed the restriction targets core First Amendment activity.
Mr. Stewart argued the law restricts intrusive calling technologies. He stated lower courts upheld this as content-neutral. He argued the debt exception is not illegal.
Chief Justice Roberts questioned the severance argument. He noted the debt exception is not illegal. He asked why severing it would help the opposing side.
Justice Breyer asked a philosophical question about content discrimination. He stated all human life involves speech. He asked counsel to define the concept.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case tests whether a federal law violates the First Amendment. The law bans automated calls to cell phones. It includes an exception for government debt collection. Political groups argue this exception favors certain speech. The government argues the law targets intrusive technology.
